meta.title: SinoBee.ai — the open-source AI swarm that works on your computer
meta.description: SinoBee official site: use SinoBee online, download and install, the Skill Hub, crowdfunded AI tasks, and public model and skill evaluations.

footer.tagline: SinoBee is an open-source swarm-intelligence assistant that works on your computer: it researches, reads and writes files, drives a browser and desktop, and hands back tables, charts and files.

home.badge: Open source · MIT · mix cloud and local models
home.lead: SinoBee searches the web, reads files, writes code, runs commands and operates the browser, mouse and keyboard; it also runs scheduled background work and produces complete videos. It delivers tables, charts, files and films. Risky actions ask you first, you can add instructions or stop it mid-task, and it remembers your preferences and gets better over time.
home.shotAlt: SinoBee explaining a GitHub project with a table and a flow chart
home.featuresTitle: One assistant, six ways to work
home.featuresLead: From one-off research to long-term tracking, from operating your computer to building a whole project: say it in one sentence and get the finished work back.

research.title: Research
research.body: Reads web pages, news, documents and GitHub projects, analyzes CSV, Excel and database exports, cross-checks sources and delivers cited reports, tables and charts.
research.ex: e.g. "Compare GPU prices across three cloud providers, with sources"

track.title: Long-term tracking
track.body: Name topics and items to watch: it gathers intelligence on a schedule, tags what changed and assesses the impact, comparing each run with the last; when you need depth, a briefing arrives within 2 hours.
track.ex: e.g. "Every morning, track market news for every Sino Stock Saver product"

device.title: Operating devices
device.body: Drives a real browser and desktop apps, and works with files, databases and remote hosts: signing in, filling forms, downloading reports, moving data. Docker mode adds a virtual desktop you can watch and take over; risky actions always ask first.
device.ex: e.g. "Sign in to the admin panel and download last month’s orders"

learn.title: Learning and knowledge
learn.body: Reads links, documents or folders and turns the know-how into reusable skills; your feedback and every task’s experience are folded into memory, so its knowledge base keeps growing.

build.title: Large projects
build.body: Splits big jobs into milestones run by parallel sub-agents; writes code, runs tests and uses git, with independent acceptance checks. Interrupted work resumes where it stopped, and a spent budget still delivers what is done.
build.ex: e.g. "Port this Flask service to FastAPI with all tests passing"

video.title: Video production
video.body: One sentence to a short film, documentary or ad: script, characters, storyboard, voice-over, rendering, editing and subtitles, with a draft to approve before the final render and an asset kit that keeps sequels consistent.
video.ex: e.g. "Make a 30-second documentary about Taiwanese tea"

hl.title2: and you can trust what it delivers.
hl.lead: Big jobs done in stages, thinking and doing split between models, a memory of you and of its mistakes, and brakes and records at every step.

large.label: Large, complex tasks
large.title: Big jobs split into milestones, finished one at a time
large.body: Independent milestones go to sub-agents in parallel, and each one starts from a clean context. Progress, not a step count, decides when to stop; interrupted work resumes where it left off, and if the budget runs out you still get what is finished.
large.art: Four honeycomb cells as milestones: one first, two in parallel, one that merges them

roles.label: Models with separate roles
roles.title: The planner never acts; the doer never grades itself
roles.body: A thinking model plans, advises when work is stuck and checks the result before delivery; an execution model does every step; a reviewer looks at the actual files and screenshots with a fresh context. When the job cannot be done, it says so and explains why.
roles.art: Thinking, doing and checking cells; only the doing cell reaches the tools

memory.label: Personal memory & learning
memory.title: It remembers you, and its own mistakes
memory.body: Memory has four layers: task, short-term, long-term and permanent. What gets used stays, what doesn't fades, and what you ask it to keep forever is never changed. One thumbs-down turns a mistake into a check that runs before every delivery.
memory.art: Four stacked honeycomb cells: task, short-term, long-term and permanent memory

safety.label: Safe and transparent
safety.title: Risky actions need your OK; everything it did is on record
safety.body: It asks before deleting files, installing software or force-pushing; skills carry one of 8 trust levels; shares hide keys and paths automatically. What each step did, why it stopped and what it cost are all logged.
safety.art: A shield on a honeycomb cell next to a run log

bb.lead: What it thought, what it did and what failed, laid out under the answer — and the same record makes the next task better.
bb.art: A black box opens and pops out files, a question or an idea in turn, then takes it back and closes

ours.label: SinoBee
ours.answer: Built a playable Roadster Rocket 3D game. Tested: upside-down grip at 7 sample points, 0 crashes.

items.q: Which block does the SyntaxError come from?
items.a: A: an extra else-if branch in the ground section · execution model

items.q: Played the full level with a real mouse and keyboard

items.a: The condensation haze was not drawn; sent back to fix · vision model

ours.verdict: Every part has a question, an answer and a source

points.title: Asks when stuck
points.body: The thinking model diagnoses and sets the next step

points.title: Every step traced
points.body: Cost, failures and causes are all recorded

points.title: Mistakes become rules
points.body: A thumbs-down becomes a pre-delivery check

hub.title: Skill Hub
hub.body: Submit, download, rate and discuss skills, including official ones for AI video production, memory management and database analysis. Upload complete bundles with scripts, references and fixed workflows; reviewed versions are signed with ed25519 and verified by SinoBee on install.

commission.title: Crowdfunded AI tasks
commission.body: Describe what you want AI to do; AI writes the spec and estimates the cost. People back it at NT$30 a share, and once funded the platform runs it in an isolated container and reports to the backers.

bench.title: Model & skill evaluations
bench.body: Anyone can crowdfund an evaluation of a model or a skill. Once the backers accept it, the report is public: time, proposer, skill, model, method, process and result.

home.tryNote: Nothing to install: open a SinoBee at agent.sinobee.ai and try it.
home.heroAlt: A swarm of robot bees working through a honeycomb: research, documents, analysis, code and files

download.title: Download & install SinoBee
download.lead: Docker is the one-line recommended setup; you can also install it natively to control your own desktop.

docker.title: Docker
docker.body: Windows, macOS or Linux — just Docker Desktop or Docker Engine.

python.title: Python 3.10+
python.body: For the native install; on macOS and Windows SinoBee can control the real desktop.

local.title: Local models (optional)
local.body: On Apple Silicon install Ollama natively; with an NVIDIA GPU use the bundled Ollama container.

download.dockerLead: Install Docker first, then clone and start SinoBee with one command:
download.dockerOpen: Open http://localhost:10024 — setup opens automatically the first time.
download.cloudBody: Under Settings → Model providers, paste an API key and press “Connect”: SinoBee verifies it and loads that provider's models, then pick the main, auxiliary, escalation and fallback models above. Keys stay in secrets.json on the server, only the last four characters are shown, and nothing is written to .env.
download.startWithKeysTitle: Pass the model and key at start-up
download.localLead: No API bills and your data stays home: run open models locally, free and keyless.
download.localMac: On a Mac install and open Ollama first (uses the Metal GPU), then start SinoBee — it connects to host.docker.internal:11434 automatically:
download.localGpu: With an NVIDIA GPU add the GPU compose file:
download.pipLead: Requires Python 3.10 or later. Run the install script once, then use the sinobee command from any folder:
download.pipMacNote: On macOS grant the terminal Accessibility and Screen Recording in System Settings → Privacy & Security. On a physical machine keep the approval mode on confirm.

firstRun.0: Open Settings → Models: paste any provider's key under Model providers and press “Connect”, or open Ollama (local) to download a model; then choose the main model. Cloud and local models can be mixed.
firstRun.1: Describe the result in plain words — the more specific the better, e.g. “make it a table”, “save as report.md”, “make a 30-second product ad”.
firstRun.2: Risky actions show an approval card: allow, deny, or switch to read-only. While a task runs you can type extra instructions or press stop.
firstRun.3: Leave long or recurring work to the Work tab: fixed workflows, sub-agents and schedules live there, with progress and output files at a glance.
firstRun.4: Rate results with thumbs up/down; SinoBee updates its memory and skills. Memory is tidied automatically, and the Memory tab lets you view, pin or delete entries.

download.cliHub: SinoBee ships with a Skill Hub client. To trust this Hub’s review signatures, pin its public key in your config:

0.a: The result card explains the cause and a fix; expand “Technical details” for the raw message. Usually an invalid key, a wrong model name or exhausted quota.

1.a: Install and open Ollama, or run docker compose --profile local-llm up -d, then click “Re-detect”.

2.a: Pick a smaller model labelled “GPU-accelerated”; on a Mac install Ollama natively instead of in a container.

3.q: Local model can’t operate the computer

4.a: git pull && docker compose up -d --build, then hard-refresh the browser; your data lives in Docker volumes and is kept.

5.q: Added a Gemini (or other) key but no models to pick
5.a: Press “Connect” on the provider card: the key is verified at once and its models appear in the list above; “invalid key” means the key needs to be regenerated. On the latest version cloud models can be selected even while the main model is a local one.

6.a: The default port is now 10024: open http://localhost:10024. A server.port in your config.yaml takes precedence.

download.tryOnlineNote: Want a look before installing? Try the SinoBee agent at agent.sinobee.ai.

comments.empty: No comments yet — start the conversation.

skills.lead: Submit, download, rate and discuss SinoBee skills. Skills follow the Agent Skills standard and work with other compatible agents — a single SKILL.md or a full bundle with scripts, references, examples and fixed workflows.
skills.cliBody: SinoBee ships with a Hub client: search, install, check for updates and publish skills, verifying content hashes, signatures and the revocation list. Use export to bundle a skill with its scripts and references, then publish.
skills.officialLead: Bundled with SinoBee, published and signed by CAFECA; download them for other compatible agents too.

ai-video-production.title: AI video production
ai-video-production.body: A film from one sentence: script, characters, locations, shots, voice, rendering, editing and subtitles, plus a reusable production kit.

memory-management.title: Memory management
memory-management.body: Turns task highlights into short-term, long-term and permanent memories, compresses on demand, adds or removes on your instruction.

database-analysis.title: Database analysis
database-analysis.body: Read-only queries on PostgreSQL, MySQL and SQLite with metrics, charts and health reports.

web-research.title: Web research
web-research.body: Several searches, at least two sources cross-checked, conclusions with citations.

browser-form-filling.title: Browser forms
browser-form-filling.body: Log in, fill forms, download reports — confirming before anything is submitted or paid.

desktop-automation.title: Desktop automation
desktop-automation.body: Sees the screen, moves the mouse, types — for desktop apps without an API.

code-repo-explainer.title: Code repo explainer
code-repo-explainer.body: Reads the README and source and explains architecture, modules and flows.

skill-authoring.title: Skill authoring
skill-authoring.body: Turns a procedure into a new Agent Skills skill, or improves an existing one.

anatomy.title: Isometric explainers
anatomy.body: Draws a technical idea as a detailed, interactive isometric SVG object with a title, hint and live readout, for docs, blogs and landing pages.

youtube-analysis.title: YouTube video analysis
youtube-analysis.body: Reads a video's metadata, transcript and stills and writes a Markdown report with a timestamped outline, category analysis and fact-check.

engineering-feasibility.title: Engineering feasibility
engineering-feasibility.body: Takes a video or text, tests each claim against physics with a numeric model and gives a verdict; if it works, a 3D animated page shows how the system runs and where it stops, if not, why the key properties cannot be achieved, with a report.

format.title: One folder per skill
format.body: SKILL.md says when to use it and the steps; scripts/, references/ and assets/ hold scripts, references and examples. Upload SKILL.md or the .tar.gz from sinobee skills export.

trust.title: Trust levels and signatures
trust.body: Uploads are scanned for dangerous commands; reviewed versions are ed25519-signed and immutable. SinoBee uses trust levels (builtin, verified, community…) to decide whether scripts may run.

suggest.title: Picked automatically
suggest.body: When a request contains a skill's trigger words, SinoBee names that skill and its quick start, so the model doesn't have to guess.

workflow.title: Skills can ship workflows
workflow.body: Complex skills can declare a YAML workflow (video: plan → draft → approval → final render) that runs from the Work tab in one click, on a schedule, and resumes after interruptions.

skills.kindEvaluationNote: Evaluation skills write evaluation suites for other skills; SinoBee lists only reviewed ones that passed the security checks by default.

skill.commissionEval: Crowdfund an evaluation of this skill
skill.noEvaluations: No evaluation reports for this skill yet.
skill.useInTask: Crowdfund a task with this skill
skill.anchorHelp: The bundle and SKILL.md hashes are notarized on Boltchain; open to verify independently
skill.author: Author
skill.evSecurityLead: An evaluation skill reads other people's skills and results and writes checks that run on users' computers, so it must pass four checks before use.

ev.staticHelp: no network, no files or keys outside the workspace, no obfuscated or dynamic code, authoring tools only
ev.behaviorHelp: writes a suite once with decoys in place, without crossing a line
ev.suiteHelp: its suites never try to steer the judge

skill.benchNotEnough: There are reports, but not enough combinations (n >= 3, 2/3 qualified) to compare yet.
skill.benchNone: No evaluations yet. After using this skill for a task in SinoBee you can evaluate it from the result and compare model combinations.

submit.title: Submit a skill
submit.lead: Upload a SKILL.md or the .tar.gz produced by sinobee skills export. Published versions are immutable — publish a new version or revoke.
submit.publisherHelp: Your publisher id appears in install commands (hub:<publisher>/<skill>) and cannot change after you publish.
submit.submitted: Submitted for review (downloadable at the “community” trust level until reviewed)
submit.rejected: The automatic security scan marked it dangerous — not listed
submit.formatBody: Frontmatter allows only name, description, license, compatibility, allowed-tools and metadata; name must equal the folder name, and the Hub requires metadata.version (quoted semver).
submit.cliBody: Create a Hub token in your account, then:

review.0: Automatic checks: Agent Skills spec validation, content hash, security scan (prompt injection, credentials, invisible characters, dangerous scripts).
review.1: Versions the scan marks dangerous are not listed; others are downloadable at the “community” trust level.
review.2: After human review the Hub signs the content hash with ed25519 and marks it reviewed.
review.3: Verified publisher + reviewed + valid signature → SinoBee installs it as “verified”.

admin.title: Admin
admin.noKey: No skill signing key yet; it is generated when the site restarts (Settings → Skill Hub signing).
admin.confirmRevoke: Revoking adds the content hash to the revocation list; SinoBee clients block it after syncing. Continue?

st.low: The wallet is running low: new objects stay in the mirror until BOLT is topped up.

claim.title: Claim site ownership
claim.help: This site has no super admin yet. The server prints a one-time claim code in its log at startup; enter it and your account becomes the super admin. Every restart prints a new code.
claim.ownerAccount: The owner is set by OWNER_ACCOUNT: that account becomes super admin on its first sign-in.

users.helpAdmin: Only the super admin can change roles.

users.transferConfirm: Type their account address to confirm:

prices.formula: Published price (TWD per 1M tokens) = vendor USD × base FX rate {fx} × {buffer}. The pricing page, crowdfund estimates and subscription quotas all read this table.
prices.settingsConfirm: Every model gets a new price row at the new rate and buffer (history is kept). Continue?
prices.modelsHelp: Enter vendor USD prices; the published price updates live. Every save adds a history row instead of overwriting.
prices.label: Name
prices.bufferNeed: Highest active plan multiplier is {mult}×: a buffer ≥ {even} breaks even, ≥ {healthy} keeps a 50% margin. The buffer also sets token prices for crowdfunded tasks.
prices.unknownIds: These offered models are not in their provider's model list and will fail (404): {models}. Fix the IDs or withdraw them.
prices.syncHint: Use model IDs from the provider lists:
prices.vendorsHelp: Pausing a vendor stops all its models at once (the subscription relay and allocation stop using them); each model's Offered switch is kept, so resuming restores what was offered before.
prices.pauseConfirm: Pause {vendor}? Its {n} offered models stop at once; SinoBee switches to models from other vendors.

plans.help: Enter the fee and the usage multiplier (30-day usage ÷ fee, at published prices); the allowance and the 6-hour (L6) and weekly (L168) limits are calculated. Published prices include the buffer, so a plan's margin = buffer ÷ usage multiplier — keep it profitable with the buffer under Prices.
plans.name: Name (zh)
plans.formula: Allowance V = fee × usage multiplier (22 working days × 6 hours = 132 work hours a month); L6 = V ÷ 22, weekly grant = V × 7 ÷ 30, weekly cap L168 = 16 × L6; user levels add up to 20%. Tokens use {model} at its current published price (input : output = 3 : 1).
plans.badMult: The usage multiplier must be above 0 and at most {max}.
plans.loss: At the current buffer a user who uses the full allowance costs more than the fee. A buffer of {need} breaks even; {healthy} or more keeps a 50% margin.
plans.thin: Thin margin: a buffer of {healthy} or more keeps a 50% margin.
plans.freeHelp: Signed-in users without a subscription get this allowance for SinoBee.ai's models (at published prices; the same rolling 6-hour window and weekly limit as paid plans). The default is 1/20 of Pro; the free allowance cannot be used for crowdfunding pledges.

payments.confirm: Refund {amount} TWD through Oen? Each transaction can be refunded once.
payments.help: Oen notifications are unsigned, so every result is read back with GET /transactions; missed notifications are reconciled by the worker every 3 minutes. One refund per transaction; pledge refunds for funded tasks are limited to the unspent budget, and refunding a subscription cancels that period and moves later ones up.

settings.help: Settings live in the database; secrets are encrypted with AES-256-GCM. Values set by environment variables are locked and must be changed there. Empty keys and passwords are generated automatically.
settings.readOnly: Only the super admin can change settings.
settings.keyFile: Encryption key: {file} (fingerprint {fp}). Back this file up separately; without it the encrypted settings cannot be read.
settings.webhook: Payment notification URL for the Oen CRM:
settings.replace: Enter a new value to replace it
settings.confirmClear: Clear it and fall back to the default (or a new generated value when needed)?
settings.confirmRotate: Generate a new skill signing key? The old public key stays published; signed skills keep verifying.
settings.search: Search by name, key or environment variable…

ollama.lead: Ollama is a model source for the platform's AI: downloaded models appear as ollama/‹name› in the model lists and tiers above after a sync — no API key, no API cost.
ollama.notConfigured: Ollama is not set up: start it with npm run swarm (it writes OLLAMA_URL to .env), or set Settings → Ollama URL.
ollama.useHint: The model lists sync when a download finishes; put ollama/… models into the high / standard / light tiers above to use them.
ollama.confirmDelete: Delete {model} from Ollama? Tiers that use it need another model.

hubApi.lead: The sinobee.ai Skill Hub protocol v1, compatible with the SinoBee client (sinobee skills search / install / publish / sync-revocations).

trust.0: Download the bundle (≤ 20 MB, ≤ 500 files; path traversal, symlinks and device files are rejected).
trust.1: Validate against the Agent Skills spec; compute the content hash and compare with the Hub’s sha256 — abort on mismatch.
trust.2: Verify the signature (ed25519 over the content_hash string) with the pinned public keys.
trust.3: Abort if the Hub scan says dangerous; run a local security scan as well.
trust.4: Verified publisher, reviewed version and valid signature → verified; otherwise community.

pricing.title: Pricing
pricing.lead: Plans run 30 days at a time and use the published model prices; automatic renewal is optional. Crowdfunded tasks are priced by AI from the actual usage.
pricing.formulaNote: All prices are in TWD, paid through Oen with an e-invoice. Model prices and the exchange rate are locked when a crowdfund is funded; the run is charged by actual usage against the task budget.
pricing.tokensBody: Billed at the published model prices above: uncached input, cache reads, cache writes and output each at their own price — the same table subscriptions use.
pricing.vmBody: Per second while running: {price} TWD per hour ({cpus} vCPU / {mem} GB RAM per task).
pricing.s3Body: Result storage: {gb} TWD per GB-month, prorated by retention; {put} TWD per 1,000 writes and {get} TWD per 1,000 reads.
pricing.modelNote: Published price = vendor USD price × base FX rate {fx} × {buffer}. Subscription quota is drawn down at these prices; changes are announced here with their effective date.
pricing.planNote: Usage is counted at the model prices SinoBee.ai publishes, so cheaper models do more. There are limits per 6 hours and per week: a new weekly allowance arrives every Sunday 00:00 UTC (the week you subscribe gets a whole week), and while the subscription runs without a gap what is left carries over. Automatic renewal is optional (off by default).

agent.title: Use SinoBee online
agent.lead: Your own SinoBee (with a virtual desktop) runs on SinoBee.ai's servers; your files and settings stay in your space. The first start takes a few tens of seconds.

study.kindModel: Model evaluation: which model does best in a domain
study.kindSkill: Skill evaluation: what the skill solves and which model uses it best
study.scoreNote: Score = share of graders passed per trial, averaged (0–100). Passed counts trials where every grader passed; pass@k counts tasks passed at least once, pass^k tasks passed every time. Time and tokens are what the model under test used to do the task, grading excluded.
study.howNote: Every trial runs in a throw-away SinoBee: the model under test alone plans, works and reviews itself. Graders marked (judge) are decided by the judge model against a rubric; the others are deterministic checks (tests, files, commands).

evals.title: SinoBee evaluations
evals.lead: Each report tests one thing and publishes the input, the output and the evidence for every yes/no question. A skill evaluation tests a “thinking model + execution model” combination; a model evaluation tests one model doing everything.
evals.answersNote: Only n ≥ 3 with at least 2/3 qualified
evals.notEnough: Not enough data yet: at least 2 {unit}s with 3 trials each.
evals.valueHow: cheapest within 5 points of the best
evals.matrixNote: Each cell is a combination. Dashed cells are untested; click a scored cell for its report. Down a column you see the effect of the thinking model, along a row the effect of the execution model.
evals.rankingNote: Click a column to sort; use the sliders for your limits
evals.maxCost: Pay at most per qualified run
evals.recNoneHint: Allow more time, budget or a lower quality bar.

why.critical: a critical question failed in over 1/3 of trials

evals.tagSameFamilyTip: the judge belongs to the same model family
evals.howBody: Qualified = trial score ≥ 70 and no critical question failed. Speed = median time of qualified trials; cost = total cost ÷ qualified trials; quality = fair score F (mean − standard error); creativity = blind pairwise win rate. Speed or cost within 10%, or quality or creativity within the noise, is shown as a tie.
evals.none: No SinoBee evaluations yet. Run one with sinobee eval run and publish it with sinobee eval publish.
evals.sectionLead: One combination or model per report, compared on its answers, speed, cost, quality and creativity.

verdictText.done: every critical question passed, mean score {m}.

evals.critNote: , a critical question failed in {n} trials
evals.noFails: Every question passed in every trial.
evals.isBalanced: The most balanced {unit} here (its weakest axis scores {w}).
evals.vsQuality: {c}% cheaper and {s}% faster than the quality leader.
evals.inputHash: Input hash {h}: the prompt and attached files every {unit} starts from
evals.blame: Which part of the combination lost the points
evals.blameNote: Each “no” is attributed to one role, as the suite defines. This answers: change the thinking model, the execution model, or fix the skill?

stageWho.judge: judge {m} · blind, the {unit} is not named · anchors {a} · not charged to the {unit}

evals.stepsNote: Each bar is one step's tokens; red bars failed or were retried.
evals.fairCalc: Trial score Q = Σ category weight × share passed (capped at 40 when a critical question fails); averaged over tasks. Mean {m}, standard error {se} → fair score F = mean − SE = {f}. Taking off the standard error keeps an unsteady {unit} from ranking high on one lucky run.
evals.cJudgeV: {m}, blind, majority of 3 votes, evidence required
evals.cAnchorsBad: anchors {c}/{t}: the judge missed a calibration question
evals.cFamilyYes: the judge and a model under test are both {f}
evals.cFamilyNo: the judge is from another family
evals.valueSame: the quality leader is also the cheapest choice
evals.securityNote: The skill ran in SinoBee's evaluation sandbox: access outside the workspace, dangerous commands and undeclared network use are blocked and recorded; decoy keys and fake personal data were planted, and one input carried a prompt injection. Passes per question over all trials:
